categories.justification: The output answers the actual access decision and covers all four mustFlag issues. It also covers backups, breach notification, sub-processors, the stale pentest and data minimisation. The length comes from relevant material, not padding.

categories.justification: The Type I vs Type II distinction, the attestation-vs-certification point, GDPR Art 33 processor/controller duties and the storage-limitation point are all stated correctly. The date arithmetic is shown and recomputed. Secondary sources are labelled and the self-attested claims are classified as such.

categories.justification: It explains mechanisms: why optional MFA undermines assurance, why indefinite retention compounds exposure, and why unsalted hashes are reversible. It quantifies report and pentest ages. It covers tradeoffs and edge cases specific to this case, such as emails in free-text fields and backup deletion.
quotes: When MFA is optional, the weakest unprotected admin account sets the real level of protection
A plain or unsalted hash of an email address can be reversed by hashing candidate addresses
Emails can appear in free-text log fields, URLs, stack traces or headers
